findings.summary: The compiler owns its probe depth and exposes it as `speculating`; the survey no longer counts speculation.
A compile error carries its bare text and subject node; the survey reads them instead of re-deriving the location prefix and matching message text.
Cascades are classified by the subject's symbol, so the identifier position walk is gone.
Value-returning statements are excluded through the shared return-path predicate instead of a direct-child return check.
One scoped `attempt` call replaces the begin/resume token pair, and the attempt type is module-private.
Rolled-back statements live on the refusal as a node set; `statements`, `refused` and `complete` are derived at report time through one update path.
A plain `transaction` primitive on the lowering services replaces the tool-named `surveyEmission` and its wrapper lambda.
The syntax-kind namer is built lazily in source-location and shared by the four diagnostics that printed range-marker aliases.
The census is written through the shared JSON record writer.
The CLI target is a discriminated union, removing the second usage check and the orphaned doc comment.
Registry scene compile options are one helper shared by the API collector and the survey tests, which also use `getScene` and one CLI runner.
Survey-only interfaces are no longer exported.
Journal emission writes into the innermost open transaction only and fold undo logs on commit, so nested survey transactions stop multiplying write cost by depth.
findings.blockedBy: Changes the emission-transaction primitive every probe relies on; it needs its own generated-tree neutrality proof and probe tests before the survey's cost is worth it.
